items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: our real piano player at that time was Fritzl, Mike Fritzl

ctx.x: If you want to hear it, you can come up and we'll dig all those things out up at Tulane, I'll show you. Some of the different stuff you got, or I can bring it down here, whatever you want.

Well, I swear, can you imagine a thing like that? And since I recorded that number, I heard all the rest of the numbers, but that one-size number I recorded. Yeah, I heard the record. Now, I heard the numbers of what we made with Jell-Ole Morton, because Jell-Ole Morton sat down and played his, you know, his compositions of Jell-Ole, and Saab and Blues, and some of that. Some of that are two or three numbers. I don't know who it was. But our real piano player at that time was Fritzl, Mike Fritzl, not Mike Fritzl.…
